+# Saved local I/O matrix replay
+
+Status: saved-evidence acceptance passed November 3. The original r17 campaign
+binds the r8 runtime. Its 9,633 completed observations and original timing
+dispositions remain immutable. This work runs no engine query.
+
+The existing collection comprises four bounded multipart bundles: metadata,
+Arrow result/reference values, original binary outputs and original text
+outputs. The maintained replay must verify the collection and declaration
+identities, reuse the existing bundle limits, and reject missing, extra,
+ambiguous or corrupted members. Original absolute paths are lookup keys inside
+the bundles, never instructions to open local files or execute archived code.
+
+Acceptance requires all of the following:
+
+- Reconcile every declared job and ordinal in the five cohorts: 205 smoke,
+  4,555 correctness, 400 fidelity, 18 lifecycle and 4,455 timing observations.
+  Reconstruct the original combined JSONL streams byte-for-byte where declared.
+- Compare complete saved Arrow results against their independent references,
+  retaining logical types, metadata, nulls, values and order. Preserve explicit
+  string/binary representation normalization and format-specific translations.
+- Reopen retained compatibility outputs with independent format readers and
+  compare all values. Validate the existing 348 Vortex readbacks against their
+  33 saved independent decode exports, bound to original output/reference and
+  provider identities. This replays those completed decodes; it does not execute
+  an archived Vortex binary or claim a newly independent Vortex decode.
+- Check output fanout count/commit evidence and every follow-on result, explicit
+  preparation/reuse, separate-process reopening and changed-source refusal.
+  Check no-fallback, caller-resource and direct-source evidence at each relevant
+  execution. Rich text wire checks must not become typed-roundtrip claims.
+- Verify source/runtime/input bindings and original process receipts/logs.
+  Replay all three historical 347-case candidates with the maintained complete
+  result comparator, keeping their original strict-gain failures and the later
+  scoped maintainer tradeoff distinct. Recompute diagnostic timing summaries
+  from the saved observations; unavailable clocks stay unavailable.
+- Exercise corruption controls and replay from a relocated packet with original
+  artifact paths unavailable. Record exact verifier/dependency identities and
+  remaining proof boundaries. Original input payloads and runtime executables
+  remain hash-bound external objects; they are unnecessary for saved-result replay.
+
+The report establishes saved-evidence completeness for this historical matrix.
+Later adaptive/table/preparation acceptance remains separate. It neither grants
+performance superiority nor closes optional adapters, remote integration, rich
+data lifecycle, competitive gates or package publication.
+
+## Accepted replay
+
+The [portable acceptance](../benchmarks/evidence/native-local-io-portable-2026-11-03/acceptance.json)
+records all 9,633 observations, 10,878 complete saved-value comparisons covering
+10,779,851 rows, and 2,648 output readbacks. Repeated observations count separately;
+the verifier decodes 75 unique Arrow pairs and 398 unique compatibility outputs.
+All 348 Vortex observations bind to their 33 previously completed independent
+Vortex decodes. The three declared combined JSONL streams reconstruct exactly.
+All three historical 347-case candidates replay their complete 12,565 result rows
+and retain `drop_no_complete_engine_gain`. The original diagnostic screen still
+contains 216 case gaps and ten family gaps. The November 1 scoped tradeoff and
+diagnostic-only decision remain separate from those original outcomes.
+
+Runtime/source binding checks cover 3,249 compiled sources, 141 external input
+and executable identities, the 289-test installed package and 202 original
+process receipts. All 65 failed and 137 passed receipts remain represented.
+Sixteen corruption-control tests pass without skips. A relocated replay passes
+after a Python audit guard rejects reads of the original evidence and source
+trees and process/network effects; two deliberate original-read controls fail,
+and the replay attempts neither original reads nor external effects. Independent
+reader dependencies load before that guard. This is an evidence-isolation check,
+not a general-purpose sandbox security claim.
+
+The maintained entrypoint is `scripts/verify_local_io_packet.py`. It uses PyArrow
+25.0.1, fastavro 1.13.1 and cramjam 2.11.0 as verification readers, outside the
+engine runtime. Run these checks with Python 3.11 or newer and those optional
+evidence dependencies.
+
+```sh
+python3 -B scripts/verify_local_io_packet.py \
+  docs/benchmarks/evidence/native-local-io-portable-2026-11-03
+python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_local_io_packet.py -v
+```

+The acceptance archive retains the three initial verifier/isolation failures,

+The collection is byte-identical to the original four bounded bundles; the

+# Where shared native execution loses useful source facts or does extra work
+
+The maintainer schedules this investigation immediately after the **1.1.0 source
+milestone and before item 19**. Keep it one work unit under the existing source,
+operator, ownership, preparation and compute-pool performance owners in the RFC
+0044 program. The first deliverable is a reproducible analysis of saved evidence.
+The analysis can select a shared mechanism, identify one measurement needed to
+select it, or close a candidate with a documented reason. [Active queue](phased-execution-plan.md#planned).
+
+## Start with complete saved operations
+
+Freeze an input index before analysis. Bind each operation to its original
+cohort, workload and ordinal, runtime and profile, source/input generation,
+artifact, resource grant, receipt, complete result and reference validation.
+Use the full stdout envelope or worker outcome when available. Compare its
+coverage with the corresponding summary. Record missing originals or malformed
+fields explicitly and preserve previous observations.
+
+Keep these sources distinct:
+
+- The fourteen-operation source-strategy probe compares original Parquet and
+  existing Vortex for the same seven queries on the checked `ci-native` parent
+  runtime. Each route has 46 independently validated rows, 24 GiB and a maximum
+  of twelve workers. [Probe and identities](native-source-strategy-investigation-2026-11-02.md).
+- The clean release runtime's fresh preparation, publication and 43 prepared
+  queries constitute a separate workflow with 381 independently validated
+  result rows. Its creation, publication and summed query engine times are
+  38.936, 0.085 and 44.580467538 seconds. Keep the earlier retained preparation
+  report used for copy attribution under its own hash and runtime. [Workflow
+  acceptance](../benchmarks/native-preparation-contracts-2026-11-02.md) ·
+  [Ownership observations](native-preparation-query-investigations-2026-11-02.md#de-source-and-preserved-run-findings).
+- The fresh 347-case cohort exposes additional analytical shapes on its own
+  five Parquet inputs with 2 GiB and two lanes. It validates 12,565 rows and
+  totals 12.006862126 engine seconds. Keep its denominator, runner, data and
+  observation independent of the seven-query probe and Full43. [Fresh 347](../benchmarks/evidence/native-preparation-fresh347-2026-11-02.json).
+
+The query runner's `execution_report()` projects selected prefixes and exact
+keys. `execution_resource_*` and `native_vortex_result_export_replay_decision_*`
+fall outside that filter. The full envelope may contain them when the route
+emits them. Inspect actual presence and applicability for each operation.
+Start with the saved files before changing either the runner or the engine.
+[Compact report](../../scripts/run_clickbench_query_uat.py) · [Process observations](../../scripts/timed_native_command.py).
+
+Produce a machine-readable operation table and a readable component ranking.
+Keep provider/route, admission and decline reasons, engine and owner timings,
+physical I/O, decode, copy/transfer, batch geometry, worker/queue and pressure
+observations alongside their units, source field and measurement scope.
+Separate process CPU, RSS, faults and block-operation counts from engine clocks,
+native reservations and physical reader bytes. Preserve observed zero, omitted,
+inapplicable and unavailable as distinct states. Deduplicate the same observation
+represented in both full and compact evidence. A resident lifetime delta needs
+the correct preceding snapshot, same owner and an uninterrupted comparison
+boundary. Peak values and overlapping work spans need their declared semantics.
+[Resident counter rules](../../scripts/native_report_evidence.py).
+

+| --- | --- | --- |

Direct Q19 and Q34 consume 12,218 batches each, up to 8,192 rows, with one input batch held. Q19/Q34 account for 66.497254751 engine seconds, 74.81% of the **net seven-query** route difference. +
+Q19 and Q34 illustrate investigation priority within the parent-runtime probe.
+The saved comparison provides no equivalent general-provider control on Vortex.
+Group findings by shared component, retain opposite-sign controls and keep
+each cohort's denominator explicit. No route-wide concurrency conclusion,
+break-even threshold or release-profile attribution follows from those two cases.
+
+## Capability decisions and finite follow-through
+
+Classify each capability opportunity using the instrumented owner boundary.
+The decision schema counts outcomes, accumulates optional observed work, and
+stores bounded reason sets. One reason appearing in a merged set does not
+establish its frequency or byte volume. Respect empty/lazy work and the scope
+of each accumulator. [Decision contract](../../shardloom-core/src/native_io_decisions.rs) ·
+[Serialization](../../shardloom-cli/src/native_decision_evidence.rs).
+
+| Observed outcome | Required disposition |
+| --- | --- |
+| Capability absent from the observation | Check workload opportunity, route and capture coverage. Mark missing attribution. |
+| Considered and legitimately declined | Preserve the semantic or resource restriction. Record its cost if measured. |
+| Declined after loss of a provable fact | Identify the producer, losing boundary, consumer and exact equivalence proof. |
+| Admitted without execution | Inspect empty input, lazy demand and actual operator work before diagnosing a wiring gap. |
+| Executed with little useful work avoided | Quantify admission, conversion and coordination cost against eligible savings. |
+| Executed with lower work and better complete-workload timing | Apply the existing correctness, resource, ownership, no-fallback and complete-cohort acceptance gates. |
+
+First rank candidates by attributable cost, demonstrated eligible work,
+coverage, confidence and remaining proof. Then add the smallest bounded
+measurement that could change a decision. Candidates include per-reason copy
+counts/bytes, per-column read/decode work, reasons weighted by applicable work,
+and existing queue fields absent from an owner report. Specify the unit,
+lifetime, overlap, reset/merge semantics and negative controls before adding
+one. An opaque owner stays unknown until its provider supplies a valid proof.
+
+Retain the demonstrated writer-digest publication path, sparse frame indexing
+and fresh Q19 minute-helper substitution. The outstanding Q19 question is
+per-column work. Q34/Q35's zero dictionary-worker counters and `not_inspected`
+physical status leave persisted frequency metadata deferred pending actual
+domain, consumer and first-use cost evidence.
+
+Acceptance is a reproducible saved-evidence analysis, a ranked component table
+and a disposition for each lane. A proposed mechanism needs a named common
+implementation owner, evidence of eligible work and a prospective complete-
+workflow check. Preserve source generation, resource ceilings, full backing
+charges, exact values/order/errors, cancellation and late output ownership.
+Preserve explicit source investment and native Vortex execution. Use the
+existing binary complete-cohort gain rule when applicable and retain earlier
+scoped tradeoffs. The initial analysis executes zero new engine queries. Any
+later timed comparison needs its own justified protocol and authorization."},{"sha":"1d06cb3aead817392cd5b965d4bc403fb62f32e3","filename":"docs/architecture/native-rich-data-lifecycle-2026-10-24.md","status":"modified","additions":4,"deletions":0,"changes":4,"blob_url":"https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/4d11d4e9c2349f0dc63dc27288b432a351c1a962/docs%2Farchitecture%2Fnative-rich-data-lifecycle-2026-10-24.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/raw/4d11d4e9c2349f0dc63dc27288b432a351c1a962/docs%2Farchitecture%2Fnative-rich-data-lifecycle-2026-10-24.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/depsilon/shardloom/contents/docs%2Farchitecture%2Fnative-rich-data-lifecycle-2026-10-24.md?ref=4d11d4e9c2349f0dc63dc27288b432a351c1a962","patch":"@@ -15,6 +15,10 @@ adds statistics, temporal fidelity, broader numeric semantics and batch function

+## Current source examples
+
+The following additions use a matching [current source build](source-checkout-install.md),
+not the published 1.0.0 package. The maintained
+[five-interface program](../../examples/source-interfaces/run.py) creates a small
+CSV, runs DataFrame, Python SQL, typed native, embedded workflow and CLI SQL queries,
+checks the same complete rows, then verifies explicit preparation and multi-output
+readback. Run it with a native Python installation and CLI from the same revision:
+
+```sh
+python examples/source-interfaces/run.py --binary /absolute/path/to/shardloom
+```
+
+It prints `status: passed`, the five interface names and rows `{"id": 2}` and
+`{"id": 3}`, and cleans its temporary files. Its 128-MiB/two-lane settings are
+illustrative caller choices. It performs no benchmark or package installation.
+
+For named scalar parameters and query-local DataFrames, use the
+[connected programming examples](../reference/connected-programming.md).
+For local Iceberg, Delta and Hudi snapshots, use the
+[table query guide](https://shardloom.io/field-guide/local-tables) and the
+[exact reader profiles](../architecture/native-local-table-readers-2026-11-02.md).
+Table sources require an explicit format, authoritative table schema and the
+appropriate selector. They cannot be treated as arbitrary Parquet directories.
+

+
+# Documentation refresh before the 1.1.0 source milestone
+
+Status: local documentation, example and rendered-site acceptance passed
+November 2. Hosted integration remains required. This closes the documentation
+work shared by phase-plan items 18 and 23; their runtime evidence and remaining
+package/integration gates retain their separate scope.
+
+The README, Python README, public status, examples and field guide distinguish
+published 1.0.0 artifacts from later source capabilities. The current-source
+sections cover connected SQL/DataFrame plans, extended analytical operations,
+direct local readers, explicit preparation, multi-output actions, adaptive
+resource decisions and finite local Iceberg/Delta/Hudi snapshot profiles.
+Catalogs, remote workflows, table commits and later rich-data lifecycle work
+retain their explicit exclusions. The website's public package identity and
+installation instructions still refer to the immutable published release.
+
+The new [source example](../../examples/source-interfaces/run.py) checks identical
+complete answers through DataFrame, Python SQL, typed native, embedded workflow
+and CLI SQL. It verifies one fanout computation, independently reopens Vortex
+and JSONL outputs, and checks explicit Vortex preparation. The field-guide
+examples also execute against the retained accepted package: all three table
+formats, named parameters/query-local relations and the connected computation.
+Table snippets substitute only small independent fixture paths/declarations.
+
+The [acceptance record](evidence/v1.1.0-documentation-refresh-2026-11-02/acceptance.json)
+binds exact commands and their original outcomes. Its compact archive retains
+54 receipts, logs, reports, helpers, screenshots and page snapshots with complete
+byte readback. Initial example mistakes and missing route-registry entries remain
+recorded alongside their corrections. Final checks pass:
+
+- Astro production build: 21 pages, Pagefind and maintained HTML aliases.
+- Astro validation: zero errors, warnings or hints.
+- Generated API/support documents, 15 API tests and ten website-link tests.
+- Four positive/negative guide/status controls, public status, website readiness,
+  static assets and an npm audit with zero reported vulnerabilities.
+- Desktop and mobile browser review: navigation, search, mobile menu, theme
+  switching and bounded code/table overflow, with no observed console errors.
+
+The separately requested [fresh 347-case observation](../benchmarks/evidence/native-preparation-fresh347-2026-11-02.json)
+passes complete independent validation of all 12,565 result rows. Its
+12.006862126-second engine total belongs to the retained preparation-contract
+runtime; this documentation change does not receive performance attribution.

+# ShardLoom 1.1.0 source milestone
+
+The 1.1.0 source package passed local acceptance on November 3 UTC. It builds
+from clean revision `ff84e23d`. Published installation instructions and channel
+proofs identify the 1.0.0 artifacts. Hosted CI and review govern integration
+of this source milestone.
+
+This minor version brings the accepted analytical, direct local I/O, adaptive
+resource and preparation work into one source package version. SQL, Python
+DataFrame, typed native, embedded workflow and CLI declarations continue to use
+the same ShardLoom engine. Vortex remains native input, state and output;
+compatibility formats use explicit readers and writers.
+
+## Changes since 1.0.0
+
+- The [connected programming model](../reference/connected-programming.md)
+  supports composing SQL and DataFrame declarations in one native plan, with
+  query-local sources, explicit parameters and retained results.
+- The [analytical program](../architecture/native-broad-query-program-2026-10-26.md)
+  adds the admitted temporal, window, relational composition and explicit batch
+  function families. Each family's type, effect and resource contracts continue
+  to govern support. Remaining program and competitive gates stay separate.
+- [Direct local I/O](../architecture/native-universal-io-implementation-2026-10-31.md)
+  shares source-demand planning and execution across all five interfaces.
+  Ordinary source queries do not depend on an automatically prepared sibling.
+  Explicit preparation retains its generation, reuse and publication contract.
+  Multiple outputs share one computation and retain independent commit/readback
+  evidence.
+- [Adaptive execution](../architecture/native-adaptive-acceptance-2026-11-02.md)
+  applies shared sizing and concurrency decisions across the declared source,
+  operator, spill and output owners within caller ceilings. Physical and
+  semantic limits remain explicit. Named reservations are not a promise of
+  complete allocator or process-memory accounting.
+- [Local table readers](../architecture/native-local-table-readers-2026-11-02.md)
+  admit finite Iceberg v1/v2, Delta and Hudi Copy-on-Write snapshot profiles.
+  Unsupported visibility, schema and file-layout combinations fail explicitly.
+  Catalog discovery, remote table access, table commits and merge-on-read
+  remain outside the admitted profiles.
+- [Preparation contracts](../benchmarks/native-preparation-contracts-2026-11-02.md)
+  reuse consumed writer proofs during immediate publication, emit sparse Zstd
+  frame offsets and preserve proven helper nullability through persistence and
+  worker admission. Shared-allocation and dictionary-frequency proposals remain
+  deferred for missing ownership/domain proof.
+
+The [documentation refresh](v1.1.0-documentation-refresh.md) supplies executable
+examples, a local-table guide and updated resource, SQL, Python and I/O guidance.
+Its desktop/mobile navigation, search and rendered-layout checks pass locally.
+
+## Compatibility and support
+
+The version change itself adds no execution behavior or machine-schema change.
+Existing documented calls keep their contract. Direct-source defaults now use
+the original source; request durable preparation explicitly when that is the
+intended workflow. The [migration reference](../reference/python-api-migration.md)
+retains transport, context ownership, typed-error and result-lifetime guidance.
+
+Python remains 3.10 or newer. Actual built wheel tags and installation proofs
+determine platform/ABI coverage. Internal Rust crates remain unpublished.
+The [schema stability contract](v1-api-schema-stability-matrix.json) and existing
+experimental/unsupported classifications remain authoritative. Unsupported
+plans fail explicitly; no external query engine supplies fallback execution.
+
+Rich-data lifecycle is planned as item 19 after the post-bump performance
+investigation. Remote authenticated workflows,
+Foundry, AI/model operations and new distribution channels retain their own
+scope and gates. This source milestone does not grant production support,
+performance superiority or broader lakehouse support.
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Run one small local workflow through all five source-build interfaces.
+
+Use a matching native Python installation and CLI from the same source revision:
+    python examples/source-interfaces/run.py --binary /absolute/path/to/shardloom
+
+The example creates and removes its own small files. It is a correctness example,
+not a benchmark. The 128-MiB allocation and two lanes are illustrative choices.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
+
+import shardloom as sl
+from shardloom import native
+
+
+EXPECTED = ({"id": 2}, {"id": 3})
+MEMORY_BYTES = 128 << 20
+LANES = 2
+
+
+def verify_rows(name, rows):
+    if tuple(rows) != EXPECTED:
+        raise AssertionError(f"{name}: expected {EXPECTED!r}, got {rows!r}")
+
+
+def verify(name, rows, fields):
+    verify_rows(name, rows)
+    for key in ("fallback_attempted", "external_engine_invoked"):
+        if fields.get(key) != "false":
+            raise AssertionError(f"{name}: missing no-fallback evidence for {key}")
+
+
+def run(binary: Path) -> None:
+    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="shardloom-source-interfaces-") as directory:
+        root = Path(directory)
+        source = root / "orders.csv"
+        source.write_text("id,amount\n1,8\n2,15\n3,21\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        schema = {"id": "int64", "amount": "int64"}
+        statement = f"SELECT id FROM '{source}' WHERE amount >= 10 ORDER BY id"
+
+        with sl.context(transport="native", memory_bytes=MEMORY_BYTES,
+                        max_parallelism=LANES) as ctx:
+            orders = ctx.read_csv(source, schema=schema)
+            selected = orders.filter(sl.col("amount") >= 10).select("id").sort("id")
+            result = selected.collect()
+            verify("DataFrame", result.to_rows(), result.details.field_map)
+
+            sql = ctx.sql(
+                "SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount >= :minimum ORDER BY id",
+                relations={"orders": orders}, parameters={"minimum": 10},
+            )
+            result = sql.collect()
+            verify("Python SQL", result.to_rows(), result.details.field_map)
+
+            # One action supplies both destinations. Each file is reopened below.
+            outputs = {"vortex": root / "selected.vortex", "jsonl": root / "selected.jsonl"}
+            written = selected.fanout(outputs)
+            if written.output_commit_status != "committed":
+                raise AssertionError("multi-output publication did not complete")
+            if written.details.field_map.get("native_vortex_result_export_execution_count") != "1":
+                raise AssertionError("multi-output action did not record one execution")
+            for kind, path in outputs.items():
+                reopened = ctx.read(path, input_format=kind).sort("id").collect()
+                verify(f"reopened {kind}", reopened.to_rows(), reopened.details.field_map)
+
+            # Ordinary reads above use the CSV directly. Durable preparation is explicit.
+            prepared = root / "orders.vortex"
+            ctx.prepare_vortex(source, prepared)
+            result = (ctx.read_vortex(prepared).filter(sl.col("amount") >= 10)
+                      .select("id").sort("id").collect())
+            verify("explicitly prepared source", result.to_rows(), result.details.field_map)
+
+        session = native.Session(native.ExecutionResources(MEMORY_BYTES, LANES))
+        arguments = ["sql", "--sql", statement, "--source-bindings", json.dumps({
+            str(source): {"input_format": "csv", "source_schema": "id:int64,amount:int64"},
+        }), "--request", "collect", "--bounded", "true",
+            "--memory-bytes", str(MEMORY_BYTES), "--max-parallelism", str(LANES)]
+        try:
+            relation = (native.Relation.scan(str(source))
+                        .filter(native.col("amount") >= native.lit(10))
+                        .project([("id", native.col("id"))])
+                        .sort([("id", False, "last")]))
+            result = session.plan(
+                relation, files=[(str(source), "csv", "id:int64,amount:int64")],
+            ).collect()
+            # Explicit Python-row export for this tiny correctness example.
+            verify("typed native", result.row_export()[0], result.report)
+
+            result = session.workflow(arguments).collect()
+            verify("embedded workflow", result.row_export()[0], result.report)
+        finally:
+            session.close()
+
+        completed = subprocess.run(
+            [str(binary), "run", *arguments, "--format", "json"],
+            check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30,
+        )
+        envelope = json.loads(completed.stdout)
+        if envelope["status"] != "success":
+            raise AssertionError(envelope)
+        # The CLI carries its fallback contract in the JSON envelope.
+        fallback = envelope["fallback"]
+        if (fallback["attempted"] is not False or fallback["allowed"] is not False
+                or fallback["engine"] is not None):
+            raise AssertionError(f"CLI SQL: invalid fallback contract: {fallback!r}")
+        fields = {row["key"]: row["value"] for row in envelope["result"]["fields"]}
+        if fields.get("result_payload_complete") != "true":
+            raise AssertionError("CLI did not return a complete result")
+        rows = [json.loads(line) for line in fields["result_jsonl"].splitlines()]
+        verify_rows("CLI SQL", rows)
+
+    print(json.dumps({"status": "passed", "interfaces": ["DataFrame", "Python SQL",
+        "typed native", "embedded workflow", "CLI SQL"], "rows": EXPECTED,
+        "multi_output_readbacks": 2, "explicit_preparation_readback": True}))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--binary", type=Path, required=True)
+    run(parser.parse_args().binary.resolve(strict=True))"},{"sha":"0b0edd9829807ed38d59a922ee55ab735ef2a58d","filename":"python/README.md","status":"modified","additions":13,"deletions":0,"changes":13,"blob_url":"https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/4d11d4e9c2349f0dc63dc27288b432a351c1a962/python%2FREADME.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/raw/4d11d4e9c2349f0dc63dc27288b432a351c1a962/python%2FREADME.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/depsilon/shardloom/contents/python%2FREADME.md?ref=4d11d4e9c2349f0dc63dc27288b432a351c1a962","patch":"@@ -71,6 +71,19 @@ writing results, and reopening a data file.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Replay the immutable r17/r8 local I/O collection without original files or engines."""
+from collections import Counter, defaultdict
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+from pathlib import Path
+import statistics
+
+from local_io_replay_values import compare, compare_wire, ipc, read_output, translated
+from native_workflow_protocol import strict_json
+from parquet_demand_completion_replay import replay as replay_347
+from query_surface.evidence import no_fallback
+from query_surface.replay import MAX_FILE, bounded_bytes, need, sha
+from query_timing_report import query_phase_timings
+from shared_performance_bundle import Bundle
+
+COLLECTION_SHA256 = '677b350b8322e3a8112417e9b4aaff37b8826fe6f669e4734a5fe112ece7f738'
+DECLARATION_SHA256 = '45cf7545e45993aa54d2b6d024de08bbb8b4418a20b33adcc3a93195b0cfcd8a'
+COUNTS = {'smoke': 205, 'correctness': 4555, 'fidelity': 400, 'timing': 4455, 'lifecycle': 18}
+SURFACES = {'cli_sql', 'embedded_workflow', 'python_sql', 'dataframe', 'typed_relation'}
+OUTPUTS = {'vortex', 'parquet', 'arrow-ipc', 'orc', 'avro', 'csv', 'json', 'jsonl'}

+class Collection:
+    """Original paths are identifiers; only the supplied packet is opened."""
+
+    def __init__(self, folder, progress=lambda message: None):
+        folder = Path(folder)
+        need(folder.is_dir() and not folder.is_symlink(), 'invalid collection directory')
+        raw = bounded_bytes(folder / 'manifest.json', MAX_FILE)
+        need(sha(raw) == COLLECTION_SHA256, 'collection identity differs')
+        index = strict_json(raw)
+        need(index['schema_version'] == 'shardloom.local_io_portable_collection.v1'
+             and [row['name'] for row in index['bundles']] == ['metadata', 'values', 'binary', 'text'],
+             'collection bundle declarations differ')
+        need({path.name for path in folder.iterdir()} - {'acceptance.json'}
+             == {'manifest.json', 'metadata', 'values', 'binary', 'text'}, 'extra collection entries')
+        self.bundles, self.paths = [], {}
+        for row in index['bundles']:
+            item = row['manifest']
+            need(item['path'] == row['name'] + '/manifest.json', 'unsafe bundle location')
+            data = bounded_bytes(folder / item['path'], MAX_FILE)
+            need((len(data), sha(data)) == (item['bytes'], item['sha256']), 'bundle manifest differs')
+            bundle = Bundle(folder / row['name'])
+            need(bundle.index['evidence']['archive_code_execution'] is False, 'archive code is not inert')
+            self.bundles.append(bundle)
+            for path in bundle.paths:
+                need(path not in self.paths, 'ambiguous path across bundles')
+                self.paths[path] = bundle
+            progress('verified bundle ' + row['name'])
+        self.declaration = self.linked(index['declaration'])
+        need(index['declaration']['sha256'] == DECLARATION_SHA256, 'declaration anchor differs')
+
+    def raw(self, path, digest=None):
+        need(path in self.paths, 'missing archived path: ' + str(path))
+        return self.paths[path].raw(path, digest)
+
+    def identity(self, item):
+        need(item['path'] in self.paths, 'missing linked archived path')
+        return self.paths[item['path']].identity(item)
+
+    def linked(self, item):
+        return strict_json(self.identity(item))
+
+
+def same(actual, expected):
+    """Float aggregates tolerate only arithmetic-rounding noise, never new clocks."""
+    if type(actual) is float and type(expected) in (int, float):
+        return math.isfinite(actual) and math.isfinite(expected) and math.isclose(actual, expected, rel_tol=0, abs_tol=1e-9)
+    if isinstance(actual, dict) and isinstance(expected, dict):
+        return actual.keys() == expected.keys() and all(same(actual[key], expected[key]) for key in actual)
+    if isinstance(actual, list) and isinstance(expected, list):
+        return len(actual) == len(expected) and all(same(a, b) for a, b in zip(actual, expected))
+    return type(actual) is type(expected) and actual == expected
+
+
+def complete_gate(gate):
+    need(gate['status'] == 'passed' and gate['returncode'] == 0
+         and gate['process_group_drained'] is True and gate['direct_child_reaped'] is True
+         and gate['timed_out'] is False and gate['interrupted_signal'] is None,
+         'required original process did not complete')
+
+
+def safe_fallback(value):
+    need(isinstance(value, dict) and value.get('attempted') is False
+         and value.get('allowed') is False and value.get('engine', 'missing') is None,
+         'unsafe or absent fallback contract')
+
+
+def refusal(record):
+    need(record.get('expected_refusal') is True, 'expected refusal was not observed')
+    evidence = record['refusal_evidence']
+    if 'envelope' in evidence:
+        envelope = evidence['envelope']
+        need(envelope['status'] == 'error', 'refusal returned success')
+        safe_fallback(envelope.get('fallback'))
+        diagnostics = envelope['diagnostics']
+    else:
+        need(evidence['external_engine_invoked'] is False, 'refusal used an external engine')
+        diagnostics = [evidence['diagnostic']]
+    need(any(d.get('code') == 'SL_INVALID_INPUT' and 'i64::MAX' in d.get('reason', '')
+             for d in diagnostics), 'unsigned refusal diagnostic differs')
+    for diagnostic in diagnostics:
+        safe_fallback(diagnostic.get('fallback'))
+    need('actual' not in record and 'readback' not in record and 'follow_on' not in record,
+         'refused write claims successful output')
+
+
+def execution(record, source, protocol):
+    fields = record['fields']
+    no_fallback(fields)
+    for key, expected in (('execution_resource_admitted_memory_bytes', protocol['memory_bytes']),
+                          ('execution_resource_admitted_max_parallelism', protocol['max_parallelism'])):
+        need(fields.get(key) == str(expected), 'caller resource admission differs: ' + key)
+    if source['format'] != 'vortex':
+        need(fields.get('native_source_demand_prepared_input_bytes_written') == '0',
+             'direct source depends on a prepared artifact')
+    targets = record['targets']
+    if targets:
+        for key, expected in (('native_vortex_result_export_execution_count', '1'),
+                              ('native_vortex_result_export_target_count', str(len(targets))),
+                              ('native_vortex_result_export_all_targets_committed', 'true')):
+            need(fields.get(key) == expected, 'writer completion differs: ' + key)
+    else:
+        need(any(key.endswith('native_io_certified') and value == 'true' for key, value in fields.items()),
+             'collection has no complete native I/O certificate')
+    timings = query_phase_timings(fields, record['process_wall_seconds'], allow_missing=bool(targets))
+    need(all(record.get(key) == value for key, value in timings.items()), 'saved clock differs from native evidence')
+    if record['case'] == 'count' and source['format'] != 'vortex':
+        metadata = source['format'] == 'parquet' and source.get('collection') not in {'hive', 'union_by_name'}
+        need(fields.get('native_source_metadata_count_sources') == ('1' if metadata else '0'),
+             'source count strategy differs')
+        if metadata:
+            for key in ('native_source_demand_projected_columns', 'native_source_demand_physical_leaf_columns',
+                        'native_source_demand_rows_decoded', 'native_source_demand_row_groups_read',
+                        'native_source_demand_data_read_bytes', 'native_source_demand_data_read_requests',
+                        'native_input_batches', 'native_input_batch_rows'):
+                need(fields.get(key) == '0', 'metadata count performed payload work')
+            need(fields.get('native_input_end_observed') == 'true', 'metadata source incomplete')
+

+class Values:
+    def __init__(self, collection, export):
+        self.collection, self.export = collection, export
+        self.pairs, self.outputs = {}, {}
+        self.comparisons = self.rows = self.readbacks = 0
+        self.vortex_observations = []
+
+    def pair(self, actual, expected):
+        key = (actual['sha256'], expected['sha256'])
+        # Hash identities are still checked on every declared link.
+        actual_bytes, expected_bytes = self.collection.identity(actual), self.collection.identity(expected)
+        if key not in self.pairs:
+            self.pairs[key] = compare(ipc(actual_bytes), ipc(expected_bytes))
+        count = self.pairs[key]
+        self.comparisons += 1
+        self.rows += count
+        return count
+
+    def readback(self, item, expected, fmt, *, rich, observation):
+        c, output = self.collection, item['output']
+        data = c.identity(output)
+        reference_bytes = c.identity(expected)
+        key = (fmt, output['sha256'], expected['sha256'], rich)
+        report = item['report']
+        if fmt == 'vortex':
+            need(all(report.get(name) is True for name in (
+                'complete_value_equality', 'native_schema_equal', 'source_generations_validated')),
+                'original Vortex comparison incomplete')
+            export_key = output['sha256'] + '-' + expected['sha256']
+            need(export_key in self.export['reports'], 'Vortex decode export missing')
+            exported = self.export['reports'][export_key]
+            self.pair(exported['actual'], expected)
+            need(exported['compared_rows'] == report['compared_rows']
+                 and exported['compared_columns'] == report['compared_columns'], 'Vortex decode coverage differs')
+            self.vortex_observations.append(dict(observation=observation, output=output,
+                                                 expected=expected, export_key=export_key))
+        else:
+            wire = rich and fmt in {'csv', 'json', 'jsonl'}
+            if wire:
+                need(report['complete_wire_values_and_order_equal'] is True
+                     and report['logical_schema_embedded'] is False
+                     and report['exact_typed_roundtrip_claim'] is False, 'rich wire scope differs')
+            else:
+                need(report['complete_values_schema_and_order_equal'] is True, 'format readback incomplete')
+                need(report['format'] == fmt and all(report[name] == output[name]
+                     for name in ('path', 'bytes', 'sha256')), 'format readback identity differs')
+            # Observations may share identical bytes and an independent decode.
+            # Each must still carry its own successful, correctly bound report.
+            if key not in self.outputs:
+                reference = ipc(reference_bytes)
+                if wire:
+                    compare_wire(data, fmt, reference)
+                else:
+                    reference = translated(reference, fmt) if rich else reference
+                    compare(read_output(data, fmt, reference.schema), reference)
+                self.outputs[key] = reference.num_rows
+            if not wire:
+                need(report['rows'] == self.outputs[key], 'format readback row count differs')
+        self.readbacks += 1
+

+def lifecycle(c, values, record, item, source, protocol):
+    prefix = 'public_workflow_preparation_'
+    for name, hit in (('prepare', 'false'), ('reuse', 'true')):
+        proof = record[name]
+        need(proof['envelope']['status'] == 'success', 'preparation/reuse failed')
+        safe_fallback(proof['envelope']['fallback'])
+        no_fallback(proof['fields'])
+        need(proof['fields'].get(prefix + 'prepared_state_reuse_hit') == hit, 'preparation reuse state differs')
+        need(proof['fields']['execution_resource_admitted_memory_bytes'] == str(protocol['memory_bytes'])
+             and proof['fields']['execution_resource_admitted_max_parallelism'] == str(protocol['max_parallelism']),
+             'preparation resources differ')
+    need(record['prepare']['fields'].get(prefix + 'input_row_count') == str(len(source['expected_rows'])),
+         'preparation did not validate the complete source')
+    c.identity(record['source_before'])
+    c.identity(record['prepared_before']['identity'])
+    child = record['separate_process']
+    need(child['status'] == 'passed' and child['pid'] != child['parent_pid']
+         and record['separate_process_call']['returncode'] == 0, 'separate-process reopening failed')
+    need(strict_json(record['separate_process_call']['stdout']) == {
+        'status': 'passed', 'pid': child['pid'], 'queries': 10}, 'separate-process stdout differs')
+    for queries, repetitions in ((record['queries'], 2), (child['queries'], 1)):
+        identities = [(row['surface'], row['case'], row['repetition']) for row in queries]
+        wanted = {(s, case, rep) for s in SURFACES for case in ('broad', 'aggregate') for rep in range(repetitions)}
+        need(len(identities) == len(wanted) and set(identities) == wanted, 'lifecycle query grid incomplete')
+        for query in queries:
+            execution(query, {'format': 'vortex'}, protocol)
+            values.pair(query['actual'], query['expected'])
+    broad = [query['expected'] for query in record['queries'] if query['case'] == 'broad']
+    need(len({(row['bytes'], row['sha256']) for row in broad}) == 1, 'prepared broad references disagree')
+    values.readback(record['independent_readback'], broad[0], 'vortex', rich=False, observation=item)
+    replacement = record['source_replacement']
+    need(replacement['before'] != replacement['after'] and replacement['identity'] == record['source_before'],
+         'generation replacement control differs')
+    rejected = record['changed_source_rejection']
+    need(rejected['envelope']['status'] == 'error', 'changed source accepted')
+    safe_fallback(rejected['envelope']['fallback'])
+    need('existing target has no matching source binding' in json.dumps(rejected).lower(),
+         'changed-source refusal diagnostic differs')
+    if record['preparation'] == 'cli_prepare':
+        need(rejected['returncode'] != 0, 'changed-source CLI succeeded')
+
+
+def stage_replay(c, name, declaration, manifest, values):
+    summary, jobs = c.linked(declaration['summary']), c.linked(declaration['jobs'])
+    size = COUNTS[name]
+    need(summary['status'] == 'passed' and summary['completed'] == summary['required'] == size
+         and summary['failures'] == [] and len(jobs) == len(declaration['observations']) == size,
+         'stage coverage incomplete: ' + name)
+    sources = {s['id']: s for group in ('small_inputs', 'bulk_inputs', 'empty_inputs', 'fidelity_inputs')
+               for s in manifest[group]}
+    digest, length, timings = hashlib.sha256(), 0, []
+    counts = Counter()
+    for ordinal, (job, item) in enumerate(zip(jobs, declaration['observations'], strict=True)):
+        record = c.linked(item)
+        need(record['status'] == 'passed' and record['ordinal'] == ordinal, 'failed or reordered observation')
+        for key, value in job.items():
+            if key in {'outputs', 'refusal'}:
+                continue
+            need(record.get(key) == value, 'job/observation mismatch: ' + key)
+        wire = (json.dumps(record, allow_nan=False, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n').encode()
+        digest.update(wire)
+        length += len(wire)
+        source = sources[record['source']]
+        if name == 'lifecycle':
+            lifecycle(c, values, record, item, source, manifest['protocol'])
+            counts['lifecycle'] += 1
+            continue
+        counts[record['surface']] += 1
+        if job.get('refusal'):
+            refusal(record)
+            counts['expected_refusals'] += 1
+            continue
+        need(not record.get('expected_refusal'), 'undeclared refusal')
+        execution(record, source, manifest['protocol'])
+        targets = record['targets']
+        need([fmt for fmt, _ in targets] == job.get('outputs', []), 'output targets differ')
+        if not targets:
+            need('actual' in record, 'collection omitted complete values')
+            values.pair(record['actual'], record['expected'])
+            counts['collections'] += 1
+        else:
+            need(all(fmt in OUTPUTS for fmt, _ in targets), 'unknown output format')
+            readbacks = [record['readback']] if name == 'fidelity' else record['readbacks']
+            follow_on = [record['follow_on']] if name == 'fidelity' else record['follow_on']
+            need(len(readbacks) == len(follow_on) == len(targets), 'output/follow-on coverage incomplete')
+            for (fmt, path), back, follow in zip(targets, readbacks, follow_on, strict=True):
+                need(back['output']['path'] == path, 'readback bound to another output')
+                values.readback(back, record['expected'], fmt, rich=name == 'fidelity', observation=item)
+                execution(follow, {'format': fmt}, manifest['protocol'])
+                values.pair(follow['actual'], follow['expected'])
+            counts['writes'] += 1
+            counts['outputs'] += len(targets)
+        if name == 'timing':
+            timings.append(record)
+    combined = declaration['combined_jsonl']
+    if combined is not None:
+        need((length, digest.hexdigest()) == (combined['bytes'], combined['sha256']),
+             'original combined observation stream differs')
+    if name != 'lifecycle':
+        need(set(SURFACES) <= counts.keys(), 'public surface omitted')
+    return dict(observations=size, coverage=dict(counts), original_jsonl_reconstructed=combined is not None), timings
+

+def timing_replay(records, protocol, saved):
+    groups, families = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list)), defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
+    for record in records:
+        target = record['targets'][0][0] if record['targets'] else None
+        groups[(record['kind'], record['source'], record['case'], target)][record['surface']].append(record)
+
+    def gap(values, cells=1):
+        fastest = min(values, key=values.get)
+        threshold = max(protocol['absolute_material_gap_seconds'] * cells,
+                        protocol['relative_material_gap'] * values[fastest])
+        return dict(values=values, fastest=fastest, threshold_seconds=threshold,
+                    gaps=[dict(surface=s, gap_seconds=v-values[fastest]) for s, v in values.items()
+                          if v-values[fastest] > threshold])
+
+    cases = []
+    for (kind, source, case, target), surfaces in groups.items():
+        need(set(surfaces) == SURFACES, 'timing surface omitted')
+        metric = 'engine_execution_seconds' if kind == 'collect' else 'complete_write_api_seconds'
+        medians = {}
+        for surface, rows in surfaces.items():
+            need(len(rows) == protocol['repetitions'] == 3
+                 and {row['repetition'] for row in rows} == {0, 1, 2}, 'timing repetitions differ')
+            numbers = [row[metric] for row in rows]
+            need(all(type(v) in (int, float) and math.isfinite(v) and v >= 0 for v in numbers), 'invalid saved clock')
+            medians[surface] = statistics.median(numbers)
+            families[(kind, case if kind == 'collect' else target, metric)][surface].append(medians[surface])
+        cases.append(dict(kind=kind, source=source, case=case, target=target, metric=metric,
+            engine_clock_available=kind == 'collect' or all(row['engine_timing_reported'] for rows in surfaces.values() for row in rows),
+            **gap(medians)))
+    family_rows = []
+    for (kind, family, metric), values in families.items():
+        counts = {len(v) for v in values.values()}
+        need(len(counts) == 1, 'timing family cells differ')
+        cells = counts.pop()
+        family_rows.append(dict(kind=kind, family=family, metric=metric, cases=cells,
+            aggregation='sum_of_per_case_medians_not_production_workload_weighting',
+            **gap({s: math.fsum(v) for s, v in values.items()}, cells)))
+    need(same(cases, saved['cases']) and same(family_rows, saved['families']), 'original timing screen differs')
+    need(sum(bool(row['gaps']) for row in cases) == saved['material_case_gaps'] == 216
+         and sum(bool(row['gaps']) for row in family_rows) == saved['material_family_gaps'] == 10,
+         'diagnostic gap disposition differs')
+    return dict(cases=len(cases), families=len(family_rows), observations=len(records),
+                material_case_gaps=216, material_family_gaps=10, disposition='diagnostic_only_by_recorded_maintainer_decision')
+

+def source_bindings(c, manifest):
+    d = c.declaration
+    external = {item['path']: item for item in d['external_artifacts']}
+    need(len(external) == len(d['external_artifacts']), 'duplicate external identity')
+
+    def bound(item):
+        if item['path'] in c.paths:
+            c.identity(item)
+        else:
+            declared = external.get(item['path'], {})
+            need(all(declared.get(key) == item[key] for key in ('path', 'bytes', 'sha256')),
+                 'unrepresented external input or executable: ' + item['path'])
+
+    runtime = c.linked(d['runtime'])
+    need(manifest['runtime'] == d['runtime'] and runtime['profile'] == 'release'
+         and runtime['features'] == ['release-user-surfaces'], 'campaign runtime binding differs')
+    root = d['artifact_root']
+    build_bytes = c.raw(root + '/' + runtime['build_receipt'])
+    need(sha(build_bytes) == runtime['build_receipt_sha256'], 'runtime build receipt differs')
+    build = strict_json(build_bytes)
+    complete_gate(build)
+    need(build['head'] == runtime['source_revision'], 'runtime source revision differs')
+    report = c.linked(d['source_verification'])
+    need(report['status'] == 'passed' and report['manifest'] == d['campaign']
+         and report['total_observations'] == sum(COUNTS.values()), 'source verification incomplete')
+    need(set(report['product_sources']) == set(runtime['source_snapshot']), 'compiled source coverage differs')
+    for name, item in report['product_sources'].items():
+        need(item['path'] == d['source_root'] + '/' + name
+             and {key: item[key] for key in ('bytes', 'sha256')} == runtime['source_snapshot'][name],
+             'compiled source identity differs')
+        c.identity(item)
+    for item in report['frozen_paths'].values():
+        bound(item)
+    for item in manifest['products']:
+        bound(item)
+        need({key: item[key] for key in ('bytes', 'sha256')} == runtime['files'][Path(item['path']).name],
+             'campaign executable differs from built runtime')
+    for before, after in zip(manifest['code'], manifest['code_snapshots'], strict=True):
+        need(c.identity(before) == c.identity(after), 'harness snapshot differs')
+    for item in manifest['package_files'] + manifest['oracle_artifacts'] + [manifest['reader']]:

+def arrow():

+    import pyarrow
+    return pyarrow

+def ipc(data):
+    pa = arrow()
+    return pa.ipc.open_file(pa.BufferReader(data)).read_all()
+
+
+def logical(table):
+    pa = arrow()
+
+    def field(value):
+        return pa.field(value.name, dtype(value.type), value.nullable, value.metadata)
+
+    def dtype(value):
+        if pa.types.is_large_string(value) or pa.types.is_string_view(value):
+            return pa.string()
+        if pa.types.is_large_binary(value) or pa.types.is_binary_view(value):
+            return pa.binary()
+        if pa.types.is_fixed_size_list(value):
+            return pa.list_(field(value.value_field), value.list_size)
+        if pa.types.is_list(value) or pa.types.is_large_list(value):
+            return pa.list_(field(value.value_field))
+        if pa.types.is_struct(value):
+            return pa.struct([field(child) for child in value])
+        return value
+
+    schema = pa.schema([field(value) for value in table.schema], table.schema.metadata)
+    return table.cast(schema)
+
+
+def compare(actual, expected):
+    actual, expected = logical(actual), logical(expected)
+    need(actual.schema.equals(expected.schema, check_metadata=True),
+         'saved logical schema/nullability/metadata differs')
+    need(actual.equals(expected), 'complete saved values or row order differ')
+    return expected.num_rows
+
+
+def translated(table, fmt):
+    """Only the original declared ORC/Avro fidelity translations are admitted."""
+    pa = arrow()
+    if fmt not in {'orc', 'avro'}:
+        return table
+
+    def dtype(value):
+        if pa.types.is_timestamp(value):
+            if fmt == 'orc':
+                return pa.timestamp('ns', 'UTC' if value.tz else None)
+            return pa.timestamp(value.unit, '+00:00' if value.tz else None)
+        if pa.types.is_list(value):
+            return pa.list_(field(value.value_field).with_name('item'))
+        if pa.types.is_struct(value):
+            return pa.struct([field(child) for child in value])
+        return value
+
+    def field(value):
+        metadata = None
+        if fmt == 'orc' and pa.types.is_timestamp(value.type):
+            metadata = {b'shardloom.arrow.timestamp.unit': value.type.unit.encode()}
+        return pa.field(value.name, dtype(value.type), True, metadata)
+
+    return table.cast(pa.schema([field(value) for value in table.schema]))
+

+def avro_fields(actual, expected):
+    need(isinstance(actual, list) and len(actual) == len(expected), 'Avro field count differs')
+    for item, field in zip(actual, expected, strict=True):
+        need(item.get('name') == field.name, 'Avro field name/order differs')
+        avro_type(item.get('type'), field)
+
+
+def avro_type(actual, expected):
+    pa = arrow()
+    choices = actual if isinstance(actual, list) else [actual]
+    nulls = [item for item in choices if item == 'null' or item == {'type': 'null'}]
+    values = [item for item in choices if item not in nulls]
+    need(len(nulls) == int(expected.nullable) and len(values) == 1, 'Avro nullability differs')
+    value, dtype = values[0], expected.type
+    wire = value.get('type') if isinstance(value, dict) else value
+    primitives = {pa.int64(): 'long', pa.int32(): 'int', pa.float64(): 'double',
+                  pa.float32(): 'float', pa.string(): 'string', pa.bool_(): 'boolean',
+                  pa.binary(): 'bytes'}
+    if dtype in primitives:
+        valid = wire == primitives[dtype] and not (isinstance(value, dict) and value.get('logicalType'))
+    elif pa.types.is_decimal128(dtype):
+        valid = (isinstance(value, dict) and wire in {'bytes', 'fixed'}
+                 and value.get('logicalType') == 'decimal' and value.get('precision') == dtype.precision
+                 and value.get('scale', 0) == dtype.scale)
+    elif pa.types.is_date32(dtype):
+        valid = isinstance(value, dict) and wire == 'int' and value.get('logicalType') == 'date'
+    elif pa.types.is_timestamp(dtype):
+        tag = ('timestamp-' if dtype.tz else 'local-timestamp-') + {
+            'ms': 'millis', 'us': 'micros', 'ns': 'nanos'}[dtype.unit]
+        valid = isinstance(value, dict) and wire == 'long' and value.get('logicalType') == tag
+    elif pa.types.is_list(dtype):
+        valid = isinstance(value, dict) and wire == 'array'
+        if valid:
+            avro_type(value['items'], dtype.value_field)
+    elif pa.types.is_struct(dtype):
+        valid = isinstance(value, dict) and wire == 'record'
+        if valid:
+            avro_fields(value.get('fields'), dtype)
+    else:
+        valid = False
+    need(valid, 'Avro physical/logical type differs')
+

+def read_output(data, fmt, schema):
+    pa = arrow()
+    stream = pa.BufferReader(data)
+    if fmt == 'parquet':
+        import pyarrow.parquet
+        return pyarrow.parquet.ParquetFile(stream).read()
+    if fmt == 'arrow-ipc':
+        return pa.ipc.open_file(stream).read_all()
+    if fmt == 'orc':
+        import pyarrow.orc
+        return pyarrow.orc.ORCFile(stream).read()
+    if fmt == 'avro':
+        import fastavro
+        reader = fastavro.reader(io.BytesIO(data))
+        avro_fields(reader.writer_schema.get('fields'), schema)
+        return pa.Table.from_pylist(list(reader), schema=schema)
+    if fmt in {'json', 'jsonl'}:
+        values = strict_json(data) if fmt == 'json' else [strict_json(line) for line in data.splitlines()]
+        need(isinstance(values, list) and all(isinstance(row, dict) and set(row) == set(schema.names)
+             for row in values), 'JSON rows/fields differ')
+        for row in values:
+            for field in schema:
+                value = row[field.name]
+                if value is None:
+                    need(field.nullable, 'unexpected JSON null')
+                elif pa.types.is_integer(field.type):
+                    need(type(value) is int, 'JSON integer type differs')
+                elif pa.types.is_floating(field.type):
+                    need(type(value) in (int, float), 'JSON floating type differs')
+                elif pa.types.is_boolean(field.type):
+                    need(type(value) is bool, 'JSON boolean type differs')
+                else:
+                    need(pa.types.is_string(field.type) and type(value) is str, 'JSON string type differs')
+        return pa.Table.from_pylist(values, schema=schema)
+    need(fmt == 'csv', 'unsupported saved output format')
+    records = csv.reader(io.StringIO(data.decode(), newline=''), strict=True)
+    need(next(records, None) == schema.names, 'CSV names/order differ')
+    rows = []
+    for cells in records:
+        need(len(cells) == len(schema), 'CSV width differs')
+        row = {}
+        for field, value in zip(schema, cells, strict=True):
+            if not value.strip() or value.strip().lower() == 'null':
+                parsed = None
+            elif pa.types.is_string(field.type):
+                parsed = value
+            elif pa.types.is_boolean(field.type):
+                need(value.lower() in {'true', 'false'}, 'invalid CSV boolean')
+                parsed = value.lower() == 'true'
+            else:
+                parsed = int(value) if pa.types.is_integer(field.type) else float(value)
+            row[field.name] = parsed
+        rows.append(row)
+    return pa.Table.from_pylist(rows, schema=schema)

+def wire_scalar(scalar, dtype):
+    pa = arrow()
+    if not scalar.is_valid:
+        return None
+    if pa.types.is_date(dtype) or pa.types.is_timestamp(dtype):
+        return scalar.value
+    if pa.types.is_decimal(dtype):
+        value = scalar.as_py().as_tuple()
+        exponent = value.exponent + dtype.scale
+        need(exponent >= 0, 'decimal scale differs')
+        coefficient = int(''.join(str(digit) for digit in value.digits)) * 10 ** exponent
+        return f'decimal128({dtype.precision},{dtype.scale}):{(-1 if value.sign else 1) * coefficient}'
+    if pa.types.is_binary(dtype):
+        return scalar.as_py().hex()
+    if pa.types.is_list(dtype):
+        return [wire_scalar(value, dtype.value_type) for value in scalar.values]
+    if pa.types.is_struct(dtype):
+        return {field.name: wire_scalar(scalar[field.name], field.type) for field in dtype}
+    return scalar.as_py()
+
+
+def compare_wire(data, fmt, expected):
+    """Rich text checks exact wire values, without claiming embedded typed schemas."""
+    pa = arrow()
+    rows = [{field.name: wire_scalar(column[row], field.type)
+             for field, column in zip(expected.schema, expected.columns, strict=True)}
+            for row in range(expected.num_rows)]
+    if fmt in {'json', 'jsonl'}:
+        actual = strict_json(data) if fmt == 'json' else [strict_json(line) for line in data.splitlines()]
+        need(exact_json(actual, rows), 'complete rich JSON wire values/order differ')

+        reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(data.decode(), newline=''), strict=True)

+        for row in rows:
+            cells = []
+            for field in expected.schema:
+                value = row[field.name]
+                if value is None:
+                    cells.append('')
+                elif pa.types.is_string(field.type):
+                    cells.append(value)
+                elif pa.types.is_binary(field.type) or pa.types.is_decimal(field.type) or pa.types.is_nested(field.type):
+                    cells.append(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')))
+                elif isinstance(value, bool):
+                    cells.append(str(value).lower())
+                else:
+                    cells.append(str(value))
+            expected_cells.append(cells)
+        need(list(reader) == expected_cells, 'complete rich CSV cells/order differ')
+    finally:
+        csv.field_size_limit(old_limit)
+

+    # Python equality alone would equate true with 1, or 1.0 with integer ticks.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Replay the saved r17 local I/O evidence without original paths or engine execution."""
+import argparse
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import sys
+
+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+sys.path[:0] = [str(REPO / 'scripts'), str(REPO / 'benchmarks/traditional_analytics')]
+from local_io_portable_replay import Collection, verify
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument('packet', type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument('--report', type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.report and args.report.exists():
+        parser.error('report already exists; preserve the previous observation')
+    progress = lambda message: print(message, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
+    report = verify(Collection(args.packet, progress), progress)
+    serialized = json.dumps(report, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + '\n'
+    if args.report:
+        with args.report.open('x') as output:
+            output.write(serialized)
+    print(serialized, end='')
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':

+---
+title: "Query local table snapshots"
+description: "Read admitted Iceberg, Delta Lake and Hudi snapshots with explicit formats and selectors."
+sidebar: {label: "Local table snapshots"}
+---
+
+import GuideVersion from '../../../components/GuideVersion.astro';
+
+<GuideVersion development />
+
+Read a table's selected state through the same SQL, DataFrame and native
+operators used for local files. Use a matching
+[current source build](https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/docs/getting-started/source-checkout-install.md)
+with `release-user-surfaces`; these readers are not in the published 1.0.0 package.
+`shardloom capabilities --format json` reports the installed reader availability
+without opening a table.
+
+## Select a table version
+
+Use `sl.read` with an explicit table format. Delta and Hudi take the local table
+root; Iceberg takes an exact metadata JSON file. This example assumes a Delta
+table with `id` and `label` columns. Replace the path and version with your own.
+The 128-MiB allocation and two lanes are illustrative caller choices.
+
+```python
+import shardloom as sl
+
+with sl.context(transport="native", memory_bytes=128 << 20,
+                max_parallelism=2) as ctx:
+    events = sl.read("/data/events", input_format="delta", version=0,
+                     client=ctx.client)
+    selected = ctx.sql(
+        "SELECT id,label FROM events WHERE id >= :minimum ORDER BY id LIMIT 20",
+        relations={"events": events}, parameters={"minimum": 2},
+    )
+    result = selected.collect()
+    print(result.schema)
+    print(result.to_rows())
+```
+
+The result contains only rows visible in version 0, with the table's logical
+column names. Filters, joins, grouping and ordering apply across its selected
+files. `to_rows()` explicitly creates Python objects for this small result.
+
+Replace the `events` declaration inside the open context for the other formats:
+
+```python
+events = sl.read("/data/iceberg/metadata.json", input_format="iceberg",
+                 snapshot_id=1, client=ctx.client)
+
+events = sl.read("/data/hudi", input_format="hudi",
+                 instant="20261101000100", client=ctx.client)
+```
+
+| Format | Selector | When omitted |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Iceberg | `snapshot_id`: signed 64-bit snapshot ID | Use the explicit metadata file's current snapshot. |
+| Delta | `version`: unsigned 64-bit log version | Freeze the latest log version seen at admission; fail if it cannot be reconstructed. |
+| Hudi | `instant`: 14- or 17-digit requested instant of a completed write | Freeze the latest completed write. An explicit instant resolves to that write's completion boundary. |
+
+Use only the selector belonging to the format. `ctx.read(path, input_format=...)`
+can declare the current table state; historical selectors are exposed by
+`sl.read(..., client=ctx.client)`. Declarations are lazy. Admission fixes the
+snapshot for the action, and later commits do not enter that held snapshot.
+An Iceberg metadata filename is explicit: the reader does not search for the
+latest metadata file or consult a catalog.
+
+## Query through the CLI
+
+Bind the same Delta table and version in a POSIX shell:
+
+```sh
+shardloom run sql \
+  --sql "SELECT id,label FROM '/data/events' WHERE id >= 2 ORDER BY id LIMIT 20" \
+  --source-bindings '{"/data/events":{"input_format":"delta","table_snapshot":{"version":0}}}' \
+  --request collect --bounded true \
+  --memory-bytes 134217728 --max-parallelism 2 --format json
+```
+
+`--bounded true` declares that the requested result fits collection; it does not
+truncate an oversized answer. Embedded workflows use the same arguments through
+`Session.workflow`. Typed callers bind
+`tables=[(path, format, snapshot_id, version, instant)]` on `Session.sql` or
+`Session.plan`, using `None` for the other selectors. See the
+[five-interface example](https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/examples/source-interfaces/run.py)
+for the shared execution and result pattern.
+
+## Supported reader profiles
+
+| Format | Admitted local state | Important exclusions |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Iceberg v1/v2 | Manifest lists/manifests, Parquet data and delete files, field-ID mapping, applicable v2 position/equality deletes, admitted primitive evolution and identity partitions. | v3/v4, encryption, unsupported types/defaults or field identity. |
+| Delta | Reader v1/v2 and explicitly admitted v3 features; contiguous JSON logs or complete classic/multipart Parquet checkpoints; add/remove reconciliation and none/name/id column mapping. | Deletion vectors, V2 checkpoints, catalog-managed tables, unsupported reader features and type widening. |
+| Hudi Copy-on-Write | Table versions 8/9, timeline layout 2, complete active timeline and local Parquet base files; completed write/replacement visibility. | Merge-on-Read, log merging, bootstrap, archived LSM history and unsupported rollback/restore/cleaned-history states. |
+
+The initial schema profile is top-level primitive data, including admitted
+numeric, text, binary, decimal, date and microsecond timestamp types. Exact
+format-specific types, evolution and partition constants follow the
+[reader contract](https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/docs/architecture/native-local-table-readers-2026-11-02.md#user-contract-and-explicit-limits).
+Nested evolution and every possible type/operator pairing are not implied.
+The table supplies its authoritative schema; `schema=` overrides and standalone
+plan schema inspection are unsupported. Inspect `result.schema` after a successful
+action. An empty valid snapshot retains its schema.
+
+## Visibility, resources and output
+
+Table visibility is applied before rows reach native operators. Missing or
+changed metadata, data or delete files fail explicitly; required deletes are
+never ignored, and uncommitted files do not enter the result. Reading every
+Parquet file in a directory is not a substitute for this contract.
+
+Metadata, delete state and physical decode workspace use the action's shared
+memory grant. Some structures must fit as a whole; reducing output rows cannot
+remove every metadata or codec allocation. See [resources](/field-guide/resources).
+
+These are local, read-only table sources. Remote paths, catalog authentication,
+`prepare_once` table ingestion and table commits are outside this route. A query
+can write an ordinary Vortex or supported compatibility result to a separate
+destination through the [existing writers](/field-guide/runtime-and-io#write-results);

+## Adaptive work in current source
+
+Current source uses the same declared grant to choose the next admitted source
+batch, conversion window, output gather, worker task or physical spill block.
+Work can shrink under shared pressure and grow again after owners release
+capacity. The engine does not raise the caller's memory or parallelism ceiling
+to make an operation fit.
+
+Physical and semantic limits remain: an IPC message, Avro block, dictionary,
+metadata structure or complete operator state may need an irreducible allocation.
+Slicing rows after decoding does not shrink that earlier decode. Where no safe
+smaller unit exists, the operation keeps its documented bound or rejects the
+allocation. A selected lane count does not prove that workers ran in parallel.
+
+Source, operator and output reports distinguish applied work from advisory
+planning. The [accepted owner matrix](https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/docs/architecture/native-adaptive-acceptance-2026-11-02.md)
+records the exact paths and pressure controls. The standalone feedback-planning
+utility remains advisory; general skew, runtime-filter and cache proposals are
+not enabled by this acceptance.

 <p>The lifecycle and <code dir="auto">Result</code> API described here is included in
 <a href="https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/docs/release/v1.0.0-release-notes.md">v1.0.0</a>. Published package availability
 is tracked in the <a href="https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/docs/release/package-channel-readiness-matrix.md">selected-channel package readiness matrix</a>.

+<div class="sl-heading-wrapper level-h2"><h2 id="current-source-capabilities">Current source capabilities</h2><a class="sl-anchor-link" href="#current-source-capabilities"><span aria-hidden="true" class="sl-anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><path d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42m8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42 1 1 0 0 0 1.42 0l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33M8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 .71.29 1 1 0 0 0 .71-.29l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42"></path></svg></span><span class="sr-only" data-pagefind-ignore="true">Section titled “Current source capabilities”</span></a></div>
+<p>The current checkout is the <a href="https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/docs/release/v1.1.0-release-notes.md">1.1.0 source milestone</a>.
+Published packages remain at 1.0.0. Build matching Python and CLI components
+from one pinned revision with <code dir="auto">release-user-surfaces</code>, and inspect that build’s
+capabilities before using a format or operator.</p>
+<table>
+<thead>
+<tr>
+<th>Task</th>
+<th>Current source support</th>
+<th>Boundary to keep explicit</th>
+</tr>
+</thead>
+<tbody>
+<tr>
+<td>Compose SQL and DataFrames</td>
+<td>Named scalar parameters, query-local relations, nested CTE scopes, admitted recursive queries and explicit CTE materialization.</td>
+<td>Parameters are values, not SQL text; recursion has declared limits. See <a href="https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/docs/reference/connected-programming.md">connected programming</a>.</td>
+</tr>
+<tr>
+<td>Analyze richer values</td>
+<td>Extended numeric/aggregate and temporal/time-series operations share typed native execution.</td>
+<td>Each operation has type, overflow, NULL and ordering rules; file adapters retain their own schema profiles.</td>
+</tr>
+<tr>
+<td>Read ordinary local sources</td>
+<td>Shared direct readers for admitted text, columnar and structured files.</td>
+<td>Durable Vortex preparation is explicit. Remote connectors are separate work. See <a href="/field-guide/execution-routes">data lifecycle</a>.</td>
+</tr>
+<tr>
+<td>Read table state</td>
+<td>Local Iceberg v1/v2, admitted Delta profiles and Hudi Copy-on-Write v8/v9.</td>
+<td>Explicit format and snapshot rules; no catalog access or table writes. See <a href="/field-guide/local-tables">local snapshots</a>.</td>
+</tr>
+<tr>
+<td>Deliver multiple outputs</td>
+<td>One supported <code dir="auto">fanout</code> action computes once and writes its requested destinations.</td>
+<td>Final publication is not a multi-file atomic transaction. See <a href="/field-guide/runtime-and-io#write-multiple-results-in-current-source">writers</a>.</td>
+</tr>
+<tr>
+<td>Adapt work to available capacity</td>
+<td>Source batches, conversion windows, queues, output gathers and native spill blocks use admitted shared headroom.</td>
+<td>Physical and semantic minimums remain; reservations are not a total-process memory cap. See <a href="/field-guide/resources#adaptive-work-in-current-source">resources</a>.</td>
+</tr>
+</tbody>
+</table>
+<p>The <a href="https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/examples/source-interfaces/run.py">five-interface example</a>
+creates a small local source, checks complete answers through DataFrame, Python
+SQL, typed native, embedded workflow and CLI SQL, then reopens two outputs and
+an explicitly prepared Vortex input. Run it with a matching native installation
+and CLI from the same source revision:</p>

+removes its temporary files. Its resource settings are examples, not workload

+<p>In current source, ordinary local queries read the original files through the shared native source
